sentences.text: Phyllodontosuchus was a small reptile belonging to the sphenosuchians, a basal group within the larger crocodylomorph lineage.

Its fossil remains include a skull and jaws featuring some unique, leaf-shaped teeth similar to those of plant-eating dinosaurs, while the front row of its mouth held five or six sharp, backward-curving teeth.

The holotype specimen is only 71.4 mm long and is imperfectly preserved. The genus was named in 2000 by Jerald Harris and colleagues, with the type species P. lufengensis named after the Lufeng Formation.
The animal lived during the Sinemurian age, between 199.5 and 192.9 million years ago.
